title: Initial Distribution System Evaluation (IDSE): purpose, applicability, the four routes, the schedule, and how subpart V monitoring locations were derived

conditions: Subpart U applies to community water systems of any size, and to nontransient noncommunity water systems serving at least 10,000 people, that use a primary or residual disinfectant other than ultraviolet light or deliver water treated with one (141.600(b))
exclusions: Nontransient noncommunity systems serving fewer than 10,000 people and transient noncommunity systems are outside subpart U; a system serving fewer than 500 people that has taken TTHM and HAA5 samples under subpart L is not required to comply unless the State says so (141.604(a))

claims.subject: What the Initial Distribution System Evaluation (IDSE) is for
claims.value: An IDSE identifies locations with representative high TTHM and HAA5 concentrations throughout the distribution system, to identify and select subpart V compliance monitoring locations; it is used in conjunction with, but separate from, subpart L compliance monitoring
conditions: IDSE results are not used to determine compliance with the MCLs in 141.64 (141.600(f))

claims.subject: The four ways a system satisfied the IDSE requirement
claims.value: Standard monitoring under 141.601, a system specific study under 141.602, a 40/30 certification under 141.603, or a very small system waiver under 141.604; the 40/30 route requires the full complement of routine (or qualifying reduced) subpart L TTHM and HAA5 compliance samples for the 141.603(a) period, the waiver requires TTHM and HAA5 samples taken under 141.131 and 141.132, and a system without the required samples conducts standard monitoring or a system specific study

claims.subject: Standard monitoring under the IDSE
claims.value: Dual sample sets at each monitoring location (one sample analyzed for TTHM, the other for HAA5), with one monitoring period during the peak historical month for TTHM or HAA5 levels or the month of warmest water temperature, determined from available compliance, study or operational data; samples at locations other than the existing subpart L monitoring locations, distributed throughout the distribution system
conditions: The number of monitoring periods and locations by source water type and population is the table in 141.601(b)(1), not quoted on this page

claims.subject: How subpart V compliance monitoring locations were recommended from the IDSE
claims.value: The IDSE report recommends and justifies where and in what months subpart V TTHM and HAA5 monitoring should be conducted, selecting the number of locations in the 141.605(b) table (used as the subpart V routine locations unless the State requires others) by the eight-step protocol of 141.605(c), each step taking a location not previously selected: (1) highest TTHM LRAA, (2) highest HAA5 LRAA, (3) the existing subpart L average residence time location (maximum residence time for ground water systems) with the highest HAA5 LRAA, (4) highest TTHM LRAA, (5) highest TTHM LRAA, (6) highest HAA5 LRAA, (7) the existing subpart L average residence time location (maximum residence time for ground water systems) with the highest TTHM LRAA, (8) highest HAA5 LRAA; repeated as necessary when more than eight locations are required, and repeated skipping steps (3) and (7) when existing subpart L results are missing or insufficient; other locations may be recommended with a rationale, and monitored if the State approves them
conditions: The location counts by source water type and population in the 141.605(b) table are not quoted on this page; the counts a system must monitor under subpart V are on page dbp.monitoring.routine

claims.subject: Timing in the recommended subpart V schedule
claims.value: Subpart V monitoring during the peak historical month for TTHM and HAA5 concentration, unless the State approves another month; a system monitoring at least quarterly schedules compliance monitoring at a regular frequency of every 90 days or fewer once the peak month is identified
